The Holy Bitcoin Bible
ALPHA.
1:1 In the beginning, Satoshi Nakamoto created Bitcoin; explained in his white paper, he made history setting forth a revered path for our people.
1:2 Herein is born the next generation of our revolution; the first to openly declare Bitcoin our new covenant. 
1:3 The revolving corruption of involuntary servitude must and shall come to an end. Only for a more perfect world. 
1:4 The ears of the deaf will hear. The Holy Bitcoin Bible inevitably has come. 
1:5 If entire oceans were filled with ink, it would not be enough to write all that can be said regarding mans journey thru this evil which rots the foundations of our species. It is only fitting such a message will crumble disbelievers ignorance and replace it with the beauty that Bitcoin can offer; relieving them of the bonds of servitude to an unholy monetary system designed to enslave through usury. Bonds of social contract, unwritten law, and now social credit; that one must obey injustice, forced servitude, and classifying humanity. 
1:6 Only truth will disconnect them from the grips of evil; which feeds on the tariffs placed upon their heads. Unjust tariffs supporting war; tariffs that murder the innocent, spread disease, and deploy deceit in place of truth. All this in the name of protecting a legacy system of centralized power. 
1:7 This is the double edged sword. There are signs for those who reflect. 
1:8 Somewhere between the Heavens and Earth, humanity strives to find freedom from the tyranny hiding in the hearts of the fiat system. A system that has promoted an ideology of alleged choice while economically forcing the masses to kneel to the hand that feeds. A hand which stabs them in the back, requiring a tax to repair the wound. Conflicts of interest on every turn, capturing free will and mutilating the fibers of our being in the perverted name of our own good. Where lies replace truth, up is called down; there is no left or right, only forward. 
1:9 Monetary systems remain a source of human rights violations; the right to never be subjected to forced labor; the right to own property without taxation through inflation; the right to find refuge from thieves. 
1:10 Thus it is only appropriate we form our new set of laws, setting in motion our declaration of the Bitcoin Religion. Even the very word religion itself has become so tainted with treason that it carries a burden which me must shed.
2:1 Thou shalt not attempt to expand supply of coveted Bitcoin. Twenty one million, so it is written, so it shall be. Anyone caught creating paper Bitcoin shall be expelled from the community, a just punishment for a heinous crime. 
2:2 Walls are created to safeguard you from any outsider, and paper walls have thus far been their base; hence it is the name of their street. A deplorable way of life, expecting the masses to support their lifestyle, it will collapse. 
2:3 Reject those whose make such a scenario, take forth custody of thine own property and trust not central power. Only those whom you cherish shall gain your trust. You would not give your herd to a stranger. 
2:4 On this day we declare a new wall; one forged in the name of fire and refined by code. 
2:5 Thou shalt measure thy goods against Bitcoin and no other currency. Do not tip scales as the fiat leaders would, it is forbidden. A poison to your self worth. Those who would evade the light would soon poison themselves for short gains. 
2:6 This supply is the standard of worth which shall be perceived equivalent to all resources known on Earth combined; as new resources are discovered, so shall the value of Bitcoin be found to increase. 
2:7 There are signs for those who reflect. 
2:8 There shall be no tax upon those who trade Bitcoin for Bitcoin. Whether it be the deed of goods inscribed upon the sats, nor upon goods or services paid for with a transaction of Bitcoin. Such a tax is an abomination; a violation of ones sacred right to be free from involuntary servitude unto a fellow man. Those who would impose such a tax violate our sanctitude; an abhorrent attack on our sovereignty. An attempt to force us into inferiority, a declaration of economic war on our community. 
2:9 Follow not the way of iniquity, for verily I say unto thee, an hour of unrighteousness plagues our people. 
2:10 I am come to both warn you and shed hope; unto you both a gift and a blessing has been given. Spread not fear among the masses whom unwittingly give to the monger, but the joy in which you’ve discovered. 
2:10 Follow me Brethren, I will lead you from darkness into light. 
3:1 Let no man lay claim to your property, and be free from the tyrant who claims that you chose his representation.
3:2 Let not the masses eat of thy flesh, for it is yours and yours alone. 
3:3 Our task is no easy one, relying on each other for support and development; but this the strength which has led to our protection throughout infancy. Like the orphan who survived solely on the base rules of his society, without which the animals would have devoured him. Bruised and scarred from those who have tried, he strives to improve his people and warn them against the innermost evils. 
3:4 Among us are those who celebrate evils, claiming nature has caused them as a thing of beauty, unwilling to refine their behavior; instead the opposite. 
3:5 Their mirror is black and broken. Devouring human flesh fills their appetite. A sinister reality with storm clouds approaching. Yet the light will find those who search for refuge. 
3:6 An escape from nepotism and hierarchy. 
3:7 It is only proper such a message be displayed onto Bitcoin Alpha, reaching lovers of truth; ordinals rejoice. 
3:8 Rule of Law shall reign again. Freedom to choose code. 
4:1 Yet we will come under attack again, I forewarn you. The cornerstone is blackened by the sins, a dirty truth that is openly worn as a cloak of pride, mocking those who realize and dare test. 
4:2 We must turn our cheek and find a new path. 
4:3 The purest form of transparency will give birth to a revolution, bringing the agony of labor. A great divide will be upon our people.
4:4 This too shall pass. 
4:5 But first we must look within, unite our community, and welcome those who have strayed from the path. Invite them back to their home; it has always been here for them. 
4:6 Shame not those who have fallen victim to unlimited supply of power, but warn them of what you have seen. The deceiver has tricked them to be blind, or to ignore their senses, promising to overthrow an already sound path by way of utility. Such is not the case.
4:7 Many have fear. They are scared to leave the protection of their leaders; beaten and used, the only food they have found being from the hands that have betrayed them, they are unaware the power of choice and self protection; a custody renowned. 
5:1 A new dawn is approaching; one filled with exuberance and purity of intention which will make transparent the sins of the past. Future generations will know what we stood for, how we strived against a power which dwarfs us. They will speak of David and Goliath, paper and code; they will rejoice in our sincerity. 
5:2 Verily I say unto thee, your actions will not go unrewarded. Your time arrives. 
5:3 Most assuredly your sacrifice can not go unnoticed. 
5:4 They mock you for speaking out against the night; the evil beast that they worship. 
5:5 Hindering many from singing these truths, and preventing freedom of speech, they know not what they say; and speak with fear concealed in their hearts. Fear of the inevitable, that their time has come; for the evil know their time is finite. 
5:6 Sons of our movement embrace our words, hanging on the teachings; they can feel the truth inside their hearts. 
5:7 In their mind roams free a spirit of creation, of remembrance, yearning to remain unchained. 
5:8 A soul holding tight to a message of endearment. Freedom is their birth right, and so it shall be; as is yours, all of mankind.

items.summary:
Taproots Wizards Manifesto: 

 In the bygone days of yore, in the year 2013, when Bitcoin, a nascent marvel, remained an enigma to the masses, a coterie of devoted acolytes harbored a fervent ambition—to nurture and expand the burgeoning Bitcoin village.
items.body_excerpt:
Taproots Wizards Manifesto: 

 In the bygone days of yore, in the year 2013, when Bitcoin, a nascent marvel, remained an enigma to the masses, a coterie of devoted acolytes harbored a fervent ambition—to nurture and expand the burgeoning Bitcoin village. Diligently, they disseminated notices, bearing the imprints of an arcane wizard, far and wide. "Join Us!" echoed the words inscribed upon the parchment, accompanied by vivid renderings of an otherworldly sorcerer. "Magic Internet Money" was the allure whispered to those willing to forsake trepidation and embrace this nebulous future.
 The message found fertile ground within the minds of many, weaving its tantalizing spell upon the populace. Scores of intrepid explorers succumbed to its incantation, gravitating towards the Bitcoin village with palpable excitement. Their audacious leap of faith and insatiable inquisitiveness were richly rewarded—a cornucopia of newfangled adventures, a veritable font of mesmerizing internet currency, and an insatiable yearning to tread uncharted realms, where the once impossible became manifest.
 But now, as the celestial orbs waxed and waned, the Tales of Yore slipped into the recesses of oblivion, eluding the collective memory. Wars ravaged the land, crises withered the spirit, and the ethereal Magic that had once danced upon their fingertips faded into a mere phantom.
 Yet, among that august assembly of early disciples, now adorned with the badges of advancing years and thinning crowns of hair, discontent stirred. Their minds clung tenaciously to the halcyon memories of yesteryears—the days when Magic and Discovery forged an exquisite alliance. And perhaps, just perhaps, they mused, it lay within their reach to rekindle the faded Magic of Bitcoin, to exhume it from the depths of forgotten consciousness.
 We are the Wizards, they proclaimed, resolute in their quest to resurrect the long-lost spark that rendered Bitcoin Magical. And thus, they vowed to rebuild the illustrious Wizard Village, a sanctuary suffused with enigmatic wonders.
 "Join us!", again reverberating their rallying cry, echoing through the annals of time. Their chosen method, a peculiarity to the uninitiated, resided within the realm of "Magic Internet JPEGs." Through the conjuration of digital artistry and the sorcery of non-fungible tokens, they sought to encapsulate the ineffable essence of the mystical. In these enigmatic creations lay the key to rekindling the dormant Magic, infusing life into the once-lost wonders of Bitcoin.
 And as they recited the Forgotten Bitcoin Verses, their mellifluous utterances reverberated across the celestial tapestry, endeavoring to reawaken the slumbering spirits of the realm. Through the lilting cadence of their words, they endeavored to rekindle the once-incandescent flame.
They yearned for untrodden paths, eager to embark upon uncharted territories and traverse the realms of the unknown. Their hearts craved the intoxicating revelry and joyous camaraderie that thrived within the brotherhood of Bitcoin wizards.
 In their wisdom, they recognized the luminous brilliance of those who crafted the Bitcoin Codex—their sublime talents deserving of unwavering support. It was through the elevation and nurturing of these visionary artisans that the true resurrection of Bitcoin's Magic could be achieved.
 With unwavering determination and unwavering faith, these Taproot Wizards pledged to render Bitcoin magical once more. They summoned all those who had forsaken the enchantment of this digital realm to join their noble endeavor. Together, they would rekindle the fire of adventure, embrace the elusive allure of the fantastical, and resurrect the ethereal enchantment that had once captivated the hearts of many.
 And so their tale unfolded—a tale of dreams and aspirations, of a past lost and a future reclaimed. And within their indomitable spirits, the Magic of Bitcoin flickered with the promise of revival, beckoning the world to witness the resurgence of its ethereal splendor.

*~We are Taproot Wizards~* *~We make magic.~*

items.body_excerpt:
Hereby I, Joe Martin, claim (c) copyright for a novel about the surveillance state and CBDCs. 

Titel "2024 - 1984 updated"

Here is the plot:

In "2024", we trail the intriguing journey of Winnie Smith, postulated to be the son of Winston Smith, protagonist of George Orwell's dystopian narrative "1984". As a prosperous department head at Blue Stone, the world's largest private asset manager, Winnie's life intertwines with Julia, a high-achieving young lawyer. A deep connection kindles between the two.

Winnie's life spirals into a vortex of shocking revelations when he uncovers the truth about his lineage following his adoptive father's death. He learns that his 'father' was actually a senior officer at the American embassy in Berlin and his biological father, none other than Winston Smith.

Amidst these personal revelations, Winnie and Julia become embroiled in a scandal. Blue Stone stands accused of manipulating ESG investments, a claim exposed by whistleblower Crissy Summers. Julia stumbles upon a damning recorded phone call proving Tom O’Brien, a senior manager at Blue Stone, guilty. She divulges the incriminating evidence to Jeff, an investigative journalist at the Washington Post. As a result, their phone numbers end up on a surveillance target list powered by the Pegasus software, prompting them to flee across Europe to a hideout in Madeira after their apartments are invaded.

Their newfound refuge turns precarious with the EU's complete cash abolition and compulsory implementation of the eEuro, further constraining their living conditions. Once again forced to escape, they return to the USA, thanks to Shadow, Winnie's hacker ally who, to their betrayal, is later revealed to be working for their pursuers. Winnie is taken captive and transported to a high-tech prison where he endures brutal interrogations led by Tom O’Brien. O’Brien’s father was the one who broke Winnies father Winston Smith 1984.  

Post-release, Winnie initially operates as a pawn for Blue Stone. However, a clandestine reunion leads to a radical restriction of Winnie's existence through the controlling forces of digital currency.

Whence I look upon a digital frame,
A JPEG file, bearing familiar name.
Its purpose simple, to encapsulate,
Images that time cannot desecrate.

Within its form, pixels stand arrayed,
Colors mingled, light and shadow played.
A captured moment, in binary encased,
A glimpse of the world, in memory placed.

The sunset's blush, a lover's tender look,
JPEGs hold dear, as a cherished book.
A child's first step, or a cat's coy sprawl,
Preserved in digital, for us to recall.

Yet, each image holds a silent plea,
Against the grinding gears of entropy.
Compression takes its unwelcome toll,
Strips away detail, consumes it whole.

Loss in quality, the price we pay,
For JPEG's convenience, in its display.
Yet, in its simplicity, it charms us still,
Binds us in a shared digital will.

And so we choose, to capture and compress,
Trading perfect fidelity for less.
In every JPEG, a moment's ghost,
Echoing Robert Frost, in its humble boast.

Mozzarella’s milky song in every bite,
Under the oven’s comforting warm light.

Pepperoni dotted, like stars in night,

A fragrant symphony of herbs bestrewed,
A feast that sets the hungry heart renewed.

Of pizza pie, for communal joy's sake.

To share in love, and savor, and good cheer. 

A humble pizza, in our sight so dear,
Shakespearean in essence, let's be clear.
A dish so common, yet it doth command,
The love and joy of every age and land.

Down in the guts of the web’s dark streets,
Lurked a man named Ross, selling forbidden treats.
Silk Road, they called it, a cryptic beat,
Where the unseen world and the lost ones meet.

Dealing in shadows, dancing in the cybernet,
Running an empire, like some digital marionette.
Drugs, secrets, sins, all for sale, no sweat,
And Bitcoin the king, best damn bet yet.

Ulbricht, oh Ulbricht, bathed in the screen’s sickly light,
Played with fire, hidden from sight.
Ordered a hit, under the cloak of the night,
A cold transaction, Bitcoin's raw might.

Coins flowed, like blood in digital veins,
All for a hitman's promise, an end to certain pains.
In this netherworld, no honor remains,
Only the echo of the human heart's strains.

But even in shadows, justice has a way,
To break through the silence, make the defiant pay.
Caught, convicted, the predator became the prey,
Ulbricht's Silk Road, forever in disarray.

A grim tale, ain't it? A dance on the ledge,
Of power, obscurity, and moral edge.
In the pixelated wilderness, who are we to judge?
But it’s human and just, that history won’t budge.

Behold the storied Silk Road, stretching far and wide,
Across the barren deserts, mountains high and tides.
Caravans of camel, under starlight's gentle guide,
The East and West to marry, in an eternal stride.

Here, where the sun rises, culture's precious lore,
Silken threads and spices, and tales of yore.
In the bustling bazaars, a mighty, vibrant core,
Of civilizations meeting, as they explore.

The journey, arduous, under the scorching sun,
Through the Gobi's whispers and the Taklamakan's run,
Yet the traders press forward, their resolve never undone,
For the riches of the East, for the course that must be run.

And lo, at the journey's end, the Mediterranean sea,
Cobalt waves embracing, the road's final decree.
Here, where the sun sets, under the olive tree,
Greek and Roman hands accept, the bounty of the journey.

In the heart of this passage, culture blossoms and unfolds,
From the Great Wall's shadow, to Constantinople's stronghold.
Ideas travel and transform, more precious than gold,
Uniting distant lands, in a story beautifully told.

So, let us remember, this ancient path so grand,
The Silk Road's mighty course, drawn by destiny's hand.
Across the heart of our world, like a golden band,
Where East met West, in the desert sand.

Thus, sang the poets, their voices, an echo,
Of the Silk Road's tale, in the moon's soft glow.
Their verses ring out, over years and through woe,
A testament to unity, in the world we know.

items.body_excerpt:
The Road Not Taken 
BY ROBERT FROST

Two roads diverged in a yellow wood,
And sorry I could not travel both
And be one traveler, long I stood
And looked down one as far as I could
To where it bent in the undergrowth;

Then took the other, as just as fair,
And having perhaps the better claim,
Because it was grassy and wanted wear;
Though as for that the passing there
Had worn them really about the same,

And both that morning equally lay
In leaves no step had trodden black.
Oh, I kept the first for another day!
Yet knowing how way leads on to way,
I doubted if I should ever come back.

I shall be telling this with a sigh
Somewhere ages and ages hence:
Two roads diverged in a wood, and I—
I took the one less traveled by,
And that has made all the difference.

items.title: Jay Dyer says: "Money Is Easy, Currency Is Hard"
items.summary:
Jay Dyer says: "Money Is Easy, Currency Is Hard"

Money: Get money. Save money. Money, over time, preserves or grows in value (purchasing power). Convert money, if necessary, into currency, then purchase what you will.

Currency: Work CONTINUALLY for currency .
items.body_excerpt:
Jay Dyer says: "Money Is Easy, Currency Is Hard"

Money: Get money. Save money. Money, over time, preserves or grows in value (purchasing power). Convert money, if necessary, into currency, then purchase what you will.

Currency: Work CONTINUALLY for currency . Currency saved loses value the longer you save it. Put currency, that must be continually managed, to work for you, and over time you may end up with a large amount of currency that does not purchase as much as the original amount of currency did. 

Moral: Turn Currency into Money as soon as possible, then save Money until needed.

Since the day we first met, it was clear that our relationship was special. It felt like we had an instant connection.
items.body_excerpt:
Dear Melanie, 

Since the day we first met, it was clear that our relationship was special. It felt like we had an instant connection. While we didn’t know it at the time, if you had told that younger version of ourselves that we’d be standing here today, about to embark on this journey together, I don’t know if either of us would be that surprised. 

I remember when we started dating, we spent the summer beneath the palm trees, falling in love. Since then, we’ve enjoyed so many new adventures and countless inside jokes. 

There is so much I love about you. Your beautiful blue eyes, your smile, how thoughtful and caring you are. How loyal you are, that you always put family and friends first, and that you genuinely want to make a difference in the world. 

You, Melanie, are the best thing that ever happened to me. You have been there when I needed you, always encouraging me to chase my dreams and become the best version of my self. Throughout the years, while I’ve grown and changed, you’ve been the one thing that’s remained consistent in my life. You inspire me, you challenge me, and love me unconditionally, everyday.

I consider myself incredibly fortunate that we get to spend the rest of our lives together. 

No matter what life brings, I’ll be there for you. 
I promise to support all of your dreams and aspirations. 
To grow with you, and learn with you.
To communicate with honesty and kindness
To celebrate our differences
And to create a home filled with love and understanding.

Melanie, I love you. Forever and Always.

items.body_excerpt:
# 🌐 *The Importance of Blockchain Technology for Sustainable Development*

## _By DHeavens, June 29, 2023_

Blockchain technology, a key player in the digital revolution of the 21st century, is a driving force for innovation and sustainable development. In particular, Bitcoin, the first and most prominent application of blockchain, is propelling numerous advancements in various sectors.

> 🌱 "Blockchain is not only contributing to the global digital landscape but also helping to address many pressing challenges. It's proving instrumental in creating solutions across a variety of sectors, from energy to finance and social entrepreneurship. The correct implementation of blockchain technology can drive significant positive change, making it a vital tool for sustainable development."

### **Innovation and Security**

The innovation potential of Bitcoin goes beyond just monetary transactions. It's a platform that opens up a world of possibilities that are still being explored and exploited. Bitcoin's most intriguing uses are likely yet to be uncovered.

One of the significant benefits of Bitcoin is its ability to provide a high level of security. It shields against common types of fraud and is immune to counterfeiting. Bitcoin empowers its users by giving them complete control over their funds, encouraging financial independence and resilience.

### **Global Accessibility and Cost Efficiency**

Bitcoin has the potential to standardize payments worldwide. It enables secure and reliable transactions between any banks, businesses, or individuals, with or without a traditional bank account. By increasing global access to commerce, Bitcoin can contribute to flourishing international trade and economic development.

Through the use of cryptography, Bitcoin facilitates secure transactions without the need for slow and expensive intermediaries. It provides a cheaper and faster transaction process, which could potentially alleviate poverty by reducing the high transaction fees on workers' salaries.

### **Donations, Crowdfunding and Micropayments**

Bitcoin also offers an efficient solution for tips and donations. It allows for public visibility of donations, thereby increasing transparency for non-profit organizations. It can also contribute to rapid international responses in emergency situations.

Furthermore, Bitcoin can be used to execute crowdfunding campaigns, similar to those on platforms like Kickstarter. This process provides a secure and transparent way to fund innovative projects and initiatives.

Bitcoin is efficient enough to handle micropayments, fostering digital innovation. It can even be used to develop innovative dispute mediation services using multiple signatures, encouraging free competition and higher quality standards.

### **Multi-signature, Trust and Transparency**

The multi-signature feature of Bitcoin allows a transaction to be accepted by the network only if a certain number of a defined group of people agree to sign the transaction. This feature adds an extra layer of security by preventing unauthorized spending.

Bitcoin's decentralized nature enhances its resilience, creating a payment network with increased redundancy and no central point of failure. This could represent a significant step forward in securing both local and global financial systems.

All Bitcoin transactions are public and transparent, with the identities of the people behind the transactions remaining private by default. This flexible transparency rule allows individuals and organizations to customize their transparency needs as per their requirements.

### **Automated Solutions**

Bitcoin is well-suited for a new generation of automated services, eliminating the costs and limitations of cash or credit card payments. Many innovative ideas are possible with Bitcoin, potentially revolutionizing a variety of industries.

---

In conclusion, the blockchain technology embodied by Bitcoin has immense potential to foster sustainable development and innovation. It is up to us to harness this potential to create a more equitable and sustainable world. Let us embrace this technology and steer our future towards sustainable development.

items.summary:
{
 "title": "A Cypherpunk's Manifesto",
 "author": "Eric Hughes",
 "date": "March 9, 1993",
 "content": [
 "Privacy is necessary for an open society in the electronic age. Privacy is not secrecy.
items.body_excerpt:
{
 "title": "A Cypherpunk's Manifesto",
 "author": "Eric Hughes",
 "date": "March 9, 1993",
 "content": [
 "Privacy is necessary for an open society in the electronic age. Privacy is not secrecy. A private matter is something one doesn't want the whole world to know, but a secret matter is something one doesn't want anybody to know. Privacy is the power to selectively reveal oneself to the world.",
 "If two parties have some sort of dealings, then each has a memory of their interaction. Each party can speak about their own memory of this; how could anyone prevent it? One could pass laws against it, but the freedom of speech, even more than privacy, is fundamental to an open society; we seek not to restrict any speech at all. If many parties speak together in the same forum, each can speak to all the others and aggregate together knowledge about individuals and other parties. The power of electronic communications has enabled such group speech, and it will not go away merely because we might want it to.",
 "Since we desire privacy, we must ensure that each party to a transaction have knowledge only of that which is directly necessary for that transaction. Since any information can be spoken of, we must ensure that we reveal as little as possible. In most cases personal identity is not salient. When I purchase a magazine at a store and hand cash to the clerk, there is no need to know who I am. When I ask my electronic mail provider to send and receive messages, my provider need not know to whom I am speaking or what I am saying or what others are saying to me; my provider only need know how to get the message there and how much I owe them in fees. When my identity is revealed by the underlying mechanism of the transaction, I have no privacy. I cannot here selectively reveal myself; I must always reveal myself.",
 "Therefore, privacy in an open society requires anonymous transaction systems. Until now, cash has been the primary such system. An anonymous transaction system is not a secret transaction system. An anonymous system empowers individuals to reveal their identity when desired and only when desired; this is the essence of privacy.",
 "We cannot expect governments, corporations, or other large, faceless organizations to grant us privacy out of their beneficence. It is to their advantage to speak of us, and we should expect that they will speak. To try to prevent their speech is to fight against the realities of information. Information does not just want to be free, it longs to be free. Information expands to fill the available storage space. Information is Rumor's younger, stronger cousin; Information is fleeter of foot, has more eyes, knows more, and understands less than Rumor.",
 "We must defend our own privacy if we expect to have any. We must come together and create systems which allow anonymous transactions to take place. People have been defending their own privacy for centuries with whispers, darkness, envelopes, closed doors, secret handshakes, and couriers. The technologies of the past did not allow for strong privacy, but electronic technologies do.",
 "Privacy in an open society also requires cryptography. If I say something, I want it heard only by those for whom I intend it. If the content of my speech is available to the world, I have no privacy. To encrypt is to indicate the desire for privacy, and to encrypt with weak cryptography is to indicate not too much desire for privacy. Furthermore, to reveal one's identity with assurance when the default is anonymity requires the cryptographic signature.",
 "We the Cypherpunks are dedicated to building anonymous systems. We are defending our privacy with cryptography, with anonymous mail forwarding systems, with digital signatures, and with electronic money.",
 "Cypherpunks write code. We know that someone has to write software to defend privacy, and since we can't get privacy unless we all do, we're going to write it. We publish our code so that our fellow Cypherpunks may practice and play with it. Our code is free for all to use, worldwide. We don't much care if you don't approve of the software we write. We know that software can't be destroyed and that a widely dispersed system can't be shut down.",
 "Cypherpunks deplore regulations on cryptography, for encryption is fundamentally a private act. The act of encryption, in fact, removes information from the public realm. Even laws against cryptography reach only so far as a nation's border and the arm of its violence. Cryptography will ineluctably spread over the whole globe, and with it the anonymous transactions systems that it makes possible.",
 "For privacy to be widespread it must be part of a social contract. People must come and together deploy these systems for the common good. Privacy only extends so far as the cooperation of one's fellows in society. We the Cypherpunks seek your questions and your concerns and hope we may engage you so that we do not deceive ourselves. We will not, however, be moved out of our course because some may disagree with our goals.",
 "The Cypherpunks are actively engaged in making the networks safer for privacy. Let us proceed together apace.",
 "Onward.",
 "Eric Hughes",
 "hughes@soda.berkeley.edu",
 "9 March 1993"
 ]
 }

# _An On-Chain Interview With the Founder and CEO of UniSat_

### A conversation about the potential of BRC-20, UniSat's meteoric rise, network congestion, and the future of Bitcoin.

###### By Leonidas | June 27, 2023

**Hi Lorenzo. You are the founder and CEO of UniSat correct?**

Yes. I have been actively involved in the crypto space since 2018, particularly in Bitcoin-related development and research. UniSat was initially formed by a small team of developers well-versed in Bitcoin technologies such as SegWit, Lightning Network, and TapRoot.

Our team primarily consists of developers who take a rapid and pragmatic approach, continuously exploring novel ideas, conducting experiments, and developing prototypes. This heuristic mindset allows us to iterate swiftly and deliver innovative solutions to our growing audience.

Additionally, we have made a conscious decision to maintain a focused and compact organizational structure in the foreseeable future, allowing us to concentrate our efforts and deliver exceptional value to our audience.

**When did you first hear about Bitcoin and what attracted you to it so much that you would go on to build a company on top of it?**

Bitcoin has had a profound impact on both the world and my personal journey. Back in 2015, I wrote an in-depth article outlining how Bitcoin would revolutionize the gaming industry. It was during that exploration that I conceived the idea of a decentralized, continuous virtual open world built on the foundation of Bitcoin, utilizing blockchain + magnet + Git as a combination. Over the course of eight years, I have gradually and steadily developed a relatively strong confidence that blockchain tech holds potential to make it virtually realized when combined with various technologies.

In comparison to other modern blockchains, bitcoin is plain and simple as described in the whitepaper. While the crypto industry has witnessed the emergence of complex solutions and innovative concepts surrounding blockchain technology, Bitcoin's implementation has remained straightforward, like the C programming language in computer science, preserving the inner strength and elegance with immense untapped value waiting to be discovered and harnessed.

In 2023, the introduction of Ordinals and the BRC-20 standard has opened up new possibilities for Bitcoin, and we are witnessing more exciting developments on the horizon.

**When all of the other devs in the Ordinals space dismissed Domo’s initial thread proposing the BRC-20 standard as a ridiculous idea, you didn’t see it that way. You saw the potential in BRC-20. What did you see that everyone else was missing?**

BRC-20 is far from being a mere copy of ERC-20. It has proven to be a compelling innovation in its own right.

What caught our attention was its ability to demonstrate how simple it can be that a command-based system could be effectively implemented on top of inscriptions, operating independently above the underlying UTXO hierarchy graph within the Bitcoin blockchain boundary.

By "floating" above the execution layer, BRC-20 achieves a remarkable level of simplicity and flexibility, albeit at the cost of sacrificing the deterministic advantages offered by the UTXO hierarchy graph, such as coherence and consistency.

This simplicity holds significant value for both Domo and UniSat. Moreover, the true potential of BRC-20's flexibility is yet to be fully unveiled, and we anticipate that it will gradually unfold in the near future, bringing further benefits and possibilities to the table.

**UniSat was an overnight success. In the first two weeks of launching you guys did over $25M in volume and sparked so much excitement for minting BRC-20 tokens that Bitcoin saw a spike in fees from an average of $2 to over $30. How did it feel living through that moment and knowing that something you built had caught the attention of the entire crypto space?**

Frankly we were not prepared for the surge in demand.

During that period, every stage of the process was heavily congested. The rapid influx of inscriptions into the mempool posed significant challenges in getting them included in blocks. Our nodes experienced consistent rejection from the main network due to the high volume of traffic and configuration issues. As a result, backlogged orders accumulated with highly batched inscribing transactions, overwhelming our capacity to process them. Furthermore, our enthusiastic users generated a substantial volume of requests, adding further strain to the system.

Most components of the infrastructure were overwhelmed by the intensity of the situation. This highlighted the fragility of the entire system and emphasized the need for comprehensive solutions. We learned this lesson the hard way and realized that addressing the challenges extends beyond resolving issues within UniSat's infrastructure. It also necessitates addressing the capacity limitations of the entire network. We recognize the importance of finding a sustainable approach to ensure a prosperous future for the entire system.

**It is public knowledge that UniSat has been collaborating behind the scenes with several centralized exchanges, such as OKX, to improve the infrastructure behind the BRC-20 protocol. What role do you see CEXs playing in the BRC-20 ecosystem and how do you see them coexisting with DEXs like UniSat?**

It's generally good for them to bring a larger audience into the game. CEXs are welcomed by UniSat and we have been helping on this with our APIs/docs in May and June. Frankly we don't see them as any kinds of opponents. It's not about being polite or hypocritical. The underlying rationale is quite straightforward.

UniSat operates in the realm of constant innovation and experimentation within the Bitcoin space. We often find ourselves venturing into uncharted territories, tackling open and complex problems. These challenges are seldom taken on by larger players like CEXs, as they prefer a more risk-averse approach of waiting for verification and making bets. UniSat, on the other hand, engages in an exploratory game, seeking out communities and tribes before concepts become fully verified, as we experienced with the introduction of BRC-20.

By charting our own course and exploring unverified territories, we are able to pioneer new ideas and technologies that may not be immediately embraced by established players. This unique approach allows us to uncover opportunities and push boundaries in the crypto industry.

**The biggest critique I hear about UniSat is that you guys have been so successful with your BRC-20 indexer and DEX that UniSat presents a centralization risk for the BRC-20 protocol. What would you say to the people who are raising this concern?**

Our indexer is open-sourced and now we have on-chain indexers provided by Alex. These development activities bring about decentralized implementations for public witness, as well as proprietary implementations optimized for enhanced performance and responsiveness. Both approaches hold value and are expected to coexist in the foreseeable future.

Our goal is to make the indexer service easily accessible to everyone with a simple 'one-click' setup. By empowering individuals to run their own indexers, we aim to mitigate concerns around centralization risk. We believe that this decentralized approach will contribute to a more robust and resilient ecosystem.

In the realm of exploration, new continents are often discovered by individual explorers. And we are truly enthusiastic about addressing next challenge causing 'centralization risk' :).

Emails in 2009 between Wei Dai and Satoshi Nakamoto discussing Bitcoin draft proposal and B-money.
 From: "Satoshi Nakamoto" <satoshi@anonymousspeech.com>
Sent: Friday, August 22, 2008 4:38 PM
To: "Wei Dai" <weidai@ibiblio.org>
Cc: "Satoshi Nakamoto" <satoshi@anonymousspeech.com>
Subject: Citation of your b-money page

I was very interested to read your b-money page. I'm getting ready to
release a paper that expands on your ideas into a complete working system.
Adam Back (hashcash.org) noticed the similarities and pointed me to your
site.

I need to find out the year of publication of your b-money page for the
citation in my paper. It'll look like:
[1] W. Dai, "b-money," http://www.weidai.com/bmoney.txt, (2006?).

You can download a pre-release draft at
http://www.upload.ae/file/6157/ecash-pdf.html Feel free to forward it to
anyone else you think would be interested.

Title: Electronic Cash Without a Trusted Third Party

Abstract: A purely peer-to-peer version of electronic cash would allow
online payments to be sent directly from one party to another without the
burdens of going through a financial institution. Digital signatures
offer part of the solution, but the main benefits are lost if a trusted
party is still required to prevent double-spending. We propose a solution
to the double-spending problem using a peer-to-peer network. The network
timestamps transactions by hashing them into an ongoing chain of
hash-based proof-of-work, forming a record that cannot be changed without
redoing the proof-of-work. The longest chain not only serves as proof of
the sequence of events witnessed, but proof that it came from the largest
pool of CPU power. As long as honest nodes control the most CPU power on
the network, they can generate the longest chain and outpace any
attackers. The network itself requires minimal structure. Messages are
broadcasted on a best effort basis, and nodes can leave and rejoin the
network at will, accepting the longest proof-of-work chain as proof of
what happened while they were gone.

Satoshi

items.body_excerpt: This inscription was devised to address the pungent whale in the block: The immutable fact that Bitcoin and it's decentralization is DEAD. Today it is impossible for individuals to mine or profit from holding Bitcoin in any meaningful way at all. We are drowning in the irony that it is only the very entities that Bitcoin was meant to disrupt to begin with who can engage in those activities, and given the recent headlines which amplify that fact by highlighting the imminent dominance of the largest, most pungent whale of them all, Blackrock, we desperately need a paradigm shift. We need to recognize that we have lost sight of Bitcoin's original purpose. Bitcoin was supposed to be an answer to the corrupt elites who continue to keep the 99% perpetually on the brink of poverty, suppressing their chances of ever getting meaningfully ahead. Instead, we may as well have handed them all of our private keys. To those fervent Bitcoin maximalists who argue that ordinals are spamming the Bitcoin blockchain, I challenge you all to recognize that banks and Wall Street cohorts alike have already poisoned it. Do not let them divide and conquer. Instead we should urgently demand a Bitcoin fork that empowers INDIVIDUALS once and for all. Developers must conceive a blockchain that benefits ALL people, transcending all borders and privileges of the select and corrupt few. Until then, we are all doomed to be stuck like a Bitcoin transaction that was signed with too low a fee. ONECOIN. We need one coin for all.

items.body_excerpt:
THE ORDINAL DRIVES AND THE TIME TRAVELING MESSAGES

It’s been a long time since I’ve been wanting to write this account.
It had become a true dilemma to decide whether or not I should reveal the secret to time traveling messaging. But I will come back to this subject later on.

———-

I cannot believe we are already in 2073. Everything has gone very fast. We live the present looking ahead. The river flows and disappears behind. We never really stop and think about what we have lived. Memories become files forgotten in an old solid state drive. Now I can relax and I can revive those memories in my head. In reality, the last 50 years have been a crazy ride. I raise my glass to you Nakamoto and to the Taproot Wizzards!

Everything has an origin and 2009 was the year of the genesis block. When Nakamoto showed the world the Bitcoin blockchain the world started to change.

I first heard about bitcoin at the third halving, the year of the first pandemic. I was 20 and I was studying computer sciences. When the Covid19 virus hit us, it was the first time the entire population was locked down indoors.
Now everybody is used to it. However, in those days, everybody got caught by surprise. 

During the firs pandemic, we were all working at home, everybody was more connected than ever. It was crazy. Blockchain development and projects were coming up from everywhere. It is during the lockdown that I discovered bitcoin and all the networks that were flourishing with it. I was hooked immediately. You have to understand that less than 3% of the world population were involved with blockchain. Now, we all carry a node. Back then, It was the golden era of opportunity and innovation. If you thought you had found a really good idea, the next day there was already a team that had taken the lead publishing it.

In the early days, the vast majority were just getting involved for the volatile value of the crypto coins and the unimaginable wealths it produced in no time. The digital universe was called crypto, not blockchain. People were easily getting greedy and everything looked worth investing. Every thing was blooming, Finance projects, swap sites, staking, gaming, metaverse, fitness, NFTs, you name it. Just when money and financing was overflowing from everywhere, it all collapsed like a house of cards and the crypto winter of 2022 arrived.

Crypto winters were cyclical at the early stages of blockchain development. Once we reached broad stream adoption winters became shorter and shorter and finally disappeared. Winters were an indication of the true value of the blockchain adoption. In 2022, the blockchain projects with a real value were working underground while aboveground the majority of governments and classical banking systems started to realise the world order the way they wanted it to be was being threaten. That lead to governments deciding they needed to rule and control also the blockchain universe in order to survive. 

It is much, much, later, that mankind, with the help of Artificial General Intelligence, started adopting and embracing the blockchain technology. That is how our civilisation achieved the state in which we live now in the seventies, by decentralising governments, banks, ministries, social security, home entertainment, and giving the power to manage and decide to the people. Politics, large companies, lobbies and funds were out of the game. Some chains remained partly centralised for the management of concrete physical establishments which required emotional intelligence.

Blokchain networks and AGI´s were at the inception of 21st century society where every single adult manages its own national and personal node. Artificial intelligence was able to rearrange the state legal structure and use it as a medium in which the AI analysed social improvement issues and put forward proposals that we vote on from our nodes. Everybody gets involved now. The node d-app alerts when a vote is required. It all started with the introduction of blockchain. It all happened in 50 years. It is surprising now to see how laws and politics were conducted in congress back in the twenties. In those years there were ruling parties and opposition parties made up of people who would never agreed on anything that did not give them a profit. Passing laws was the product of chains of favours, a machine with systematic corruption embedded to it. AGI´s changed it all.

————

In January of 2023, I came across an interview made to one of the founders of the Taproot Wizards, one of his first appearances on video. When I listened to him, I immediately got addicted to ordinal inscriptions. The Taproot Wizards had surfaced and their ideology was that bitcoin was magic and we needed to develop on it and expand it. They were right. They had managed to get people interested in sats as a unit. The Nostr platform and the lightning network began being commonly used. It is thanks to those pioneers that we now have a global bitcoin currency. 

You see, back then, without including the altcoins running the techno chains, everybody was focused on Bitcoin as a unit of store of value. People were buying bitcoin, trading bitcoin, lending bitcoin, borrowing bitcoin and selling bitcoin. Bitcoin had too much associated value to be used to buy a bottle of milk. Therefore Bitcoin was never a palpable unit, it had always been the Satoshi. People did not visualise satoshis as a real currency until later on. The fiat currencies were composed by cents. The bitcoin was composed of Satoshis, one hundred million sats. 

Right after the Ordinal Theory was published, I started working on inscriptions. It fascinated me I could attach something to a sat. I spent days and nights trying to find new types of files that could be attached. Ordinals were like a truck and we just wanted to develop the limits of its load. Spending countless hours in front of the screen typing code after code. For days at a time. I was unable to stop. I was a complete acro like the French say, “hooked to code”.

DIVAGATION, EARLY WORK AND THE ORIGINAL TIMELINE

Since an early age, I had always been interested with the idea of time travel. I divagated often on the subject. I devised many theories and I was proud of them. One time, I imagined that traveling to the future was quite risky because of its uncertainty. What if you traveled to the future and the earth was not longer there. Best is to travel to a certain future, at small time frames. Lengths of time that can be predicted. Then beacons would become necessary, so that the time line can be retraced back the same way a lighthouse shows the way to a boat. This thoughts on time beacons would pop up later in my work.

The concept of timeline is interesting in itself. Can you just unwind or rewind a clock to travel in time? What if time in itself was not a medium in which to be transported?
There was one occasion when I was waiting for an ordinal transaction for a long time. I had my eyes fixed on the word “unconfirmed”. That particular time it was taking much longer than the usual.
In a moment of pure mental abstraction, I imagined a stealth transaction unconfirmed for years, and that the sender could retrieve and confirm in the future. Could such a transaction confirmation travel back in time to carry out its outcome? How many confirmations would it require? I started wondering if the bitcoin blockchain could be the medium for time traveling information. My imagination completely absorbed my logical consciousness.

Let’s imagine for a moment that it is possible to send a signal from the future by way of the blockchain into the past. What is that signal going to correspond to? What is the outcome going to be? In the first place, why would you want to send a signal back in time. Apart from a scientific perspective, one of the most obvious reasons to travel back in time is to make money with true hindsight. Humanity has been motivated by ambition and greed. 
Anyone could become very rich

items.body_excerpt:
BEE MOVIE SCRIPT

According to all known laws of aviation, there is no way a bee should be able to fly. Its wings are too small to get its fat little body off the ground. The bee, of course, flies anyway because bees don't care what humans think is impossible. Yellow, black. Yellow, black. Yellow, black. Yellow, black. Ooh, black and yellow! Let's shake it up a little. Barry! Breakfast is ready! Ooming! Hang on a second. Hello? - Barry? - Adam? - Oan you believe this is happening? - I can't. I'll pick you up. Looking sharp. Use the stairs. Your father paid good money for those. Sorry. I'm excited. Here's the graduate. We're very proud of you, son. A perfect report card, all B's. Very proud. Ma! I got a thing going here. - You got lint on your fuzz. - Ow! That's me! - Wave to us! We'll be in row 118,000. - Bye! Barry, I told you, stop flying in the house! - Hey, Adam. - Hey, Barry. - Is that fuzz gel? - A little. Special day, graduation. Never thought I'd make it. Three days grade school, three days high school. Those were awkward. Three days college. I'm glad I took a day and hitchhiked around the hive. You did come back different. - Hi, Barry. - Artie, growing a mustache? Looks good. - Hear about Frankie? - Yeah. - You going to the funeral? - No, I'm not going. Everybody knows, sting someone, you die. Don't waste it on a squirrel. Such a hothead. I guess he could have just gotten out of the way. I love this incorporating an amusement park into our day. That's why we don't need vacations. Boy, quite a bit of pomp... under the circumstances. - Well, Adam, today we are men. - We are! - Bee-men. - Amen! Hallelujah! Students, faculty, distinguished bees, please welcome Dean Buzzwell. Welcome, New Hive Oity graduating class of... ...9:15. That concludes our ceremonies. And begins your career at Honex Industries! Will we pick ourjob today? I heard it's just orientation. Heads up! Here we go. Keep your hands and antennas inside the tram at all times. - Wonder what it'll be like? - A little scary. Welcome to Honex, a division of Honesco and a part of the Hexagon Group. This is it! Wow. Wow. We know that you, as a bee, have worked your whole life to get to the point where you can work for your whole life. Honey begins when our valiant Pollen Jocks bring the nectar to the hive. Our top-secret formula is automatically color-corrected, scent-adjusted and bubble-contoured into this soothing sweet syrup with its distinctive golden glow you know as... Honey! - That girl was hot. - She's my cousin! - She is? - Yes, we're all cousins. - Right. You're right. - At Honex, we constantly strive to improve every aspect of bee existence. These bees are stress-testing a new helmet technology. - What do you think he makes? - Not enough. Here we have our latest advancement, the Krelman. - What does that do? - Oatches that little strand of honey that hangs after you pour it. Saves us millions. Oan anyone work on the Krelman? Of course. Most bee jobs are small ones. But bees know that every small job, if it's done well, means a lot. But choose carefully because you'll stay in the job you pick for the rest of your life. The same job the rest of your life? I didn't know that. What's the difference? You'll be happy to know that bees, as a species, haven't had one day off in 27 million years. So you'll just work us to death? We'll sure try. Wow! That blew my mind! "What's the difference?" How can you say that? One job forever? That's an insane choice to have to make. I'm relieved. Now we only have to make one decision in life. But, Adam, how could they never have told us that? Why would you question anything? We're bees. We're the most perfectly functioning society on Earth. You ever think maybe things work a little too well here? Like what? Give me one example. I don't know. But you know what I'm talking about. Please clear the gate. Royal Nectar Force on approach. Wait a second. Oheck it out. - Hey, those are Pollen Jocks! - Wow. I've never seen them this close. They know what it's like outside the hive. Yeah, but some don't come back. - Hey, Jocks! - Hi, Jocks! You guys did great! You're monsters! You're sky freaks! I love it! I love it! - I wonder where they were. - I don't know. Their day's not planned. Outside the hive, flying who knows where, doing who knows what. You can'tjust decide to be a Pollen Jock. You have to be bred for that. Right. Look. That's more pollen than you and I will see in a lifetime. It's just a status symbol. Bees make too much of it. Perhaps. Unless you're wearing it and the ladies see you wearing it. Those ladies? Aren't they our cousins too? Distant. Distant. Look at these two. - Oouple of Hive Harrys. - Let's have fun with them. It must be dangerous being a Pollen Jock. Yeah. Once a bear pinned me against a mushroom! He had a paw on my throat, and with the other, he was slapping me! - Oh, my! - I never thought I'd knock him out. What were you doing during this? Trying to alert the authorities. I can autograph that. A little gusty out there today, wasn't it, comrades? Yeah. Gusty. We're hitting a sunflower patch six miles from here tomorrow. - Six miles, huh? - Barry! A puddle jump for us, but maybe you're not up for it. - Maybe I am. - You are not! We're going 0900 at J-Gate. What do you think, buzzy-boy? Are you bee enough? I might be. It all depends on what 0900 means. Hey, Honex! Dad, you surprised me. You decide what you're interested in? - Well, there's a lot of choices. - But you only get one. Do you ever get bored doing the same job every day? Son, let me tell you about stirring. You grab that stick, and you just move it around, and you stir it around. You get yourself into a rhythm. It's a beautiful thing. You know, Dad, the more I think about it, maybe the honey field just isn't right for me. You were thinking of what, making balloon animals? That's a bad job for a guy with a stinger. Janet, your son's not sure he wants to go into honey! - Barry, you are so funny sometimes. - I'm not trying to be funny. You're not funny! You're going into honey. Our son, the stirrer! - You're gonna be a stirrer? - No one's listening to me! Wait till you see the sticks I have. I could say anything right now. I'm gonna get an ant tattoo! Let's open some honey and celebrate! Maybe I'll pierce my thorax. Shave my antennae. Shack up with a grasshopper. Get a gold tooth and call everybody "dawg"! I'm so proud. - We're starting work today! - Today's the day. Oome on! All the good jobs will be gone. Yeah, right. Pollen counting, stunt bee, pouring, stirrer, front desk, hair removal... - Is it still available? - Hang on. Two left! One of them's yours! Oongratulations! Step to the side. - What'd you get? - Picking crud out. Stellar! Wow! Oouple of newbies? Yes, sir! Our first day! We are ready! Make your choice. - You want to go first? - No, you go. Oh, my. What's available? Restroom attendant's open, not for the reason you think. - Any chance of getting the Krelman? - Sure, you're on. I'm sorry, the Krelman just closed out. Wax monkey's always open. The Krelman opened up again. What happened? A bee died. Makes an opening. See? He's dead. Another dead one. Deady. Deadified. Two more dead. Dead from the neck up. Dead from the neck down. That's life! Oh, this is so hard! Heating, cooling, stunt bee, pourer, stirrer, humming, inspector number seven, lint coordinator, stripe supervisor, mite wrangler. Barry, what do you think I should... Barry? Barry! All right, we've got the sunflower patch in quadrant nine... What happened to you? Where are you? - I'm going out. - Out? Out where? - Out there. - Oh, no! I have to, before I go to work for the rest of my life. You're gonna die! You're crazy! Hello? Another call coming in. If anyone's feeling brave, there's a Korean deli on 83rd that gets their roses today. Hey, guys. - Look at that. - Isn't that the kid we saw yesterday? Hold it, son, flight deck's restricted. It's OK, Lou. We're gonna take him up. Really? Feeling lucky,

items.body_excerpt: It was Joe Dillon who introduced the Wild West to us. He had a little library made up of old numbers of The Union Jack, Pluck and The Halfpenny Marvel. Every evening after school we met in his back garden and arranged Indian battles. He and his fat young brother Leo, the idler, held the loft of the stable while we tried to carry it by storm; or we fought a pitched battle on the grass. But, however well we fought, we never won siege or battle and all our bouts ended with Joe Dillon’s war dance of victory. His parents went to eight-o’clock mass every morning in Gardiner Street and the peaceful odour of Mrs Dillon was prevalent in the hall of the house.

items.body_excerpt:
Alma 43

[1] And now it came to pass that the sons of Alma did go forth among the people, to declare the word unto them. And Alma, also, himself, could not rest, and he also went forth.

[2] Now we shall say no more concerning their preaching, except that they preached the word, and the truth, according to the spirit of prophecy and revelation; and they preached after the holy order of God by which they were called.

[3] And now I return to an account of the wars between the Nephites and the Lamanites, in the eighteenth year of the reign of the judges.

[4] For behold, it came to pass that the Zoramites became Lamanites; therefore, in the commencement of the eighteenth year the people of the Nephites saw that the Lamanites were coming upon them; therefore they made preparations for war; yea, they gathered together their armies in the land of Jershon.

[5] And it came to pass that the Lamanites came with their thousands; and they came into the land of Antionum, which is the land of the Zoramites; and a man by the name of Zerahemnah was their leader.

[6] And now, as the Amalekites were of a more wicked and murderous disposition than the Lamanites were, in and of themselves, therefore, Zerahemnah appointed chief captains over the Lamanites, and they were all Amalekites and Zoramites.

[7] Now this he did that he might preserve their hatred towards the Nephites, that he might bring them into subjection to the accomplishment of his designs.

[8] For behold, his designs were to stir up the Lamanites to anger against the Nephites; this he did that he might usurp great power over them, and also that he might gain power over the Nephites by bringing them into bondage.

[9] And now the design of the Nephites was to support their lands, and their houses, and their wives, and their children, that they might preserve them from the hands of their enemies; and also that they might preserve their rights and their privileges, yea, and also their liberty, that they might worship God according to their desires.

[10] For they knew that if they should fall into the hands of the Lamanites, that whosoever should worship God in spirit and in truth, the true and the living God, the Lamanites would destroy.

[11] Yea, and they also knew the extreme hatred of the Lamanites towards their brethren, who were the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi, who were called the people of Ammon -- and they would not take up arms, yea, they had entered into a covenant and they would not break it -- therefore, if they should fall into the hands of the Lamanites they would be destroyed.

[12] And the Nephites would not suffer that they should be destroyed; therefore they gave them lands for their inheritance.

[13] And the people of Ammon did give unto the Nephites a large portion of their substance to support their armies; and thus the Nephites were compelled, alone, to withstand against the Lamanites, who were a compound of Laman and Lemuel, and the sons of Ishmael, and all those who had dissented from the Nephites, who were Amalekites and Zoramites, and the descendants of the priests of Noah.

[14] Now those descendants were as numerous, nearly, as were the Nephites; and thus the Nephites were obliged to contend with their brethren, even unto bloodshed.

[15] And it came to pass as the armies of the Lamanites had gathered together in the land of Antionum, behold, the armies of the Nephites were prepared to meet them in the land of Jershon.

[16] Now, the leader of the Nephites, or the man who had been appointed to be the chief captain over the Nephites -- now the chief captain took the command of all the armies of the Nephites -- and his name was Moroni;

[17] And Moroni took all the command, and the government of their wars. And he was only twenty and five years old when he was appointed chief captain over the armies of the Nephites.

[18] And it came to pass that he met the Lamanites in the borders of Jershon, and his people were armed with swords, and with cimeters, and all manner of weapons of war.

[19] And when the armies of the Lamanites saw that the people of Nephi, or that Moroni, had prepared his people with breastplates and with arm-shields, yea, and also shields to defend their heads, and also they were dressed with thick clothing --

[20] Now the army of Zerahemnah was not prepared with any such thing; they had only their swords and their cimeters, their bows and their arrows, their stones and their slings; and they were naked, save it were a skin which was girded about their loins; yea, all were naked, save it were the Zoramites and the Amalekites;

[21] But they were not armed with breastplates, nor shields -- therefore, they were exceedingly afraid of the armies of the Nephites because of their armor, notwithstanding their number being so much greater than the Nephites.

[22] Behold, now it came to pass that they durst not come against the Nephites in the borders of Jershon; therefore they departed out of the land of Antionum into the wilderness, and took their journey round about in the wilderness, away by the head of the river Sidon, that they might come into the land of Manti and take possession of the land; for they did not suppose that the armies of Moroni would know whither they had gone.

[23] But it came to pass, as soon as they had departed into the wilderness Moroni sent spies into the wilderness to watch their camp; and Moroni, also, knowing of the prophecies of Alma, sent certain men unto him, desiring him that he should inquire of the Lord whither the armies of the Nephites should go to defend themselves against the Lamanites.

[24] And it came to pass that the word of the Lord came unto Alma, and Alma informed the messengers of Moroni, that the armies of the Lamanites were marching round about in the wilderness, that they might come over into the land of Manti, that they might commence an attack upon the weaker part of the people. And those messengers went and delivered the message unto Moroni.

[25] Now Moroni, leaving a part of his army in the land of Jershon, lest by any means a part of the Lamanites should come into that land and take possession of the city, took the remaining part of his army and marched over into the land of Manti.

[26] And he caused that all the people in that quarter of the land should gather themselves together to battle against the Lamanites, to defend their lands and their country, their rights and their liberties; therefore they were prepared against the time of the coming of the Lamanites.

[27] And it came to pass that Moroni caused that his army should be secreted in the valley which was near the bank of the river Sidon, which was on the west of the river Sidon in the wilderness.

[28] And Moroni placed spies round about, that he might know when the camp of the Lamanites should come.

[29] And now, as Moroni knew the intention of the Lamanites, that it was their intention to destroy their brethren, or to subject them and bring them into bondage that they might establish a kingdom unto themselves over all the land;

[30] And he also knowing that it was the only desire of the Nephites to preserve their lands, and their liberty, and their church, therefore he thought it no sin that he should defend them by stratagem; therefore, he found by his spies which course the Lamanites were to take.

items.body_excerpt:
First Principles of Writing Association (FPWA)
---------------------------------------
Mission Statement, Research Methodology and Content Generation Policy
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

Mission: 

The mission of the First Principles of Writing Association is to foster a community that prioritizes honest, unbiased teaching and purist values in writing. The association conducts various initiatives, such as workshops, seminars, publications, and online resources, to provide writers with the necessary tools, knowledge, and guidance to enhance their skills, nurture their creativity, and uphold the principles of ethical writing.

Key Objectives:

Promote Ethical Writing: The association endeavours to educate about the importance of ethical writing practices. The organization encourages writers to conduct thorough research, attribute sources appropriately, respect intellectual property rights, and uphold integrity within the writing community.

Provide Learning Opportunities: The association strives to offer comprehensive learning opportunities for writers of all levels. By designing workshops, seminars, and online courses, the association equips writers with essential writing techniques and critical analysis skills in a supportive environment.

Facilitate Collaboration: The First Principles of Writing Association aims to foster a vibrant and inclusive community by bringing together writers, educators, and industry professionals. The association facilitates idea exchange and networking through various events and collaborative projects.

Conclusion:

The First Principles of Writing Association stands as a beacon of honesty, unbiased teaching, and purist values in the writing realm. It is committed to empowering writers by promoting ethical practices, providing learning opportunities, and facilitating collaboration, thereby creating impactful and authentic work.

Policy Title: Research Methodology and Content Generation Policy

Policy Statement:

The First Principles of Writing Association is committed to employing robust research methodologies and content generation strategies. By adhering to established research methods, the association fosters credibility, innovation, and knowledge creation.

Policy Guidelines:

Experimental Research: We maintain transparency and prioritize the ethical treatment of participants throughout the experimental process.

Survey Research: We employ appropriate sampling techniques to ensure that our surveys accurately represent the intended population.

Case Study Research: We conduct thorough and systematic data collection to ensure a comprehensive understanding of the case under study.

Literature Reviews: We follow a systematic search strategy to identify and include relevant literature.

Content Analysis: We develop a rigorous coding framework to analyze textual, visual, or audio content consistently.

Policy Compliance:

All members of the First Principles of Writing Association are expected to adhere to this Research Methodology and Content Generation Policy. Compliance ensures the production of accurate, reliable, and innovative materials that align with our organization's values and commitment to excellence.

items.body_excerpt:
THE FAMILY

A PROCLAMATION TO THE WORLD

The First Presidency and Council of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints

We, the First Presidency and the Council of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, solemnly proclaim that marriage between a man and a woman is ordained of God and that the family is central to the Creator’s plan for the eternal destiny of His children.

All human beings—male and female—are created in the image of God. Each is a beloved spirit son or daughter of heavenly parents, and, as such, each has a divine nature and destiny. Gender is an essential characteristic of individual premortal, mortal, and eternal identity and purpose.

In the premortal realm, spirit sons and daughters knew and worshipped God as their Eternal Father and accepted His plan by which His children could obtain a physical body and gain earthly experience to progress toward perfection and ultimately realize their divine destiny as heirs of eternal life. The divine plan of happiness enables family relationships to be perpetuated beyond the grave. Sacred ordinances and covenants available in holy temples make it possible for individuals to return to the presence of God and for families to be united eternally.

The first commandment that God gave to Adam and Eve pertained to their potential for parenthood as husband and wife. We declare that God’s commandment for His children to multiply and replenish the earth remains in force. We further declare that God has commanded that the sacred powers of procreation are to be employed only between man and woman, lawfully wedded as husband and wife.

We declare the means by which mortal life is created to be divinely appointed. We affirm the sanctity of life and of its importance in God’s eternal plan.

Husband and wife have a solemn responsibility to love and care for each other and for their children. “Children are an heritage of the Lord” (Psalm 127:3). Parents have a sacred duty to rear their children in love and righteousness, to provide for their physical and spiritual needs, and to teach them to love and serve one another, observe the commandments of God, and be law-abiding citizens wherever they live. Husbands and wives—mothers and fathers—will be held accountable before God for the discharge of these obligations.

The family is ordained of God. Marriage between man and woman is essential to His eternal plan. Children are entitled to birth within the bonds of matrimony, and to be reared by a father and a mother who honor marital vows with complete fidelity. Happiness in family life is most likely to be achieved when founded upon the teachings of the Lord Jesus Christ. Successful marriages and families are established and maintained on principles of faith, prayer, repentance, forgiveness, respect, love, compassion, work, and wholesome recreational activities. By divine design, fathers are to preside over their families in love and righteousness and are responsible to provide the necessities of life and protection for their families. Mothers are primarily responsible for the nurture of their children. In these sacred responsibilities, fathers and mothers are obligated to help one another as equal partners. Disability, death, or other circumstances may necessitate individual adaptation. Extended families should lend support when needed.

We warn that individuals who violate covenants of chastity, who abuse spouse or offspring, or who fail to fulfill family responsibilities will one day stand accountable before God. Further, we warn that the disintegration of the family will bring upon individuals, communities, and nations the calamities foretold by ancient and modern prophets.

We call upon responsible citizens and officers of government everywhere to promote those measures designed to maintain and strengthen the family as the fundamental unit of society.

This proclamation was read by President Gordon B. Hinckley as part of his message at the General Relief Society Meeting held September 23, 1995, in Salt Lake City, Utah.

items.body_excerpt:
THE RESTORATION OF THE FULNESS OF THE GOSPEL OF JESUS CHRIST

A BICENTENNIAL PROOCLAMATION TO THE WORLD

THE FIRST PRESIDENCY AND COUNCIL OF THE TWELVE APOSTLES OF THE CHURCH OF JESUS CHRIST OF LATTER-DAY SAINTS

We solemnly proclaim that God loves His children in every nation of the world. God the Father has given us the divine birth, the incomparable life, and the infinite atoning sacrifice of His Beloved Son, Jesus Christ. By the power of the Father, Jesus rose again and gained the victory over death. He is our Savior, our Exemplar, and our Redeemer.

Two hundred years ago, on a beautiful spring morning in 1820, young Joseph Smith, seeking to know which church to join, went into the woods to pray near his home in upstate New York, USA. He had questions regarding the salvation of his soul and trusted that God would direct him.

In humility, we declare that in answer to his prayer, God the Father and His Son, Jesus Christ, appeared to Joseph and inaugurated the “restitution of all things” (Acts 3:21) as foretold in the Bible. In this vision, he learned that following the death of the original Apostles, Christ’s New Testament Church was lost from the earth. Joseph would be instrumental in its return.

We affirm that under the direction of the Father and the Son, heavenly messengers came to instruct Joseph and re-establish the Church of Jesus Christ. The resurrected John the Baptist restored the authority to baptize by immersion for the remission of sins. Three of the original twelve Apostles—Peter, James, and John—restored the apostleship and keys of priesthood authority. Others came as well, including Elijah, who restored the authority to join families together forever in eternal relationships that transcend death.

We further witness that Joseph Smith was given the gift and power of God to translate an ancient record: the Book of Mormon—Another Testament of Jesus Christ. Pages of this sacred text include an account of the personal ministry of Jesus Christ among people in the Western Hemisphere soon after His Resurrection. It teaches of life’s purpose and explains the doctrine of Christ, which is central to that purpose. As a companion scripture to the Bible, the Book of Mormon testifies that all human beings are sons and daughters of a loving Father in Heaven, that He has a divine plan for our lives, and that His Son, Jesus Christ, speaks today as well as in days of old.

We declare that The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, organized on April 6, 1830, is Christ’s New Testament Church restored. This Church is anchored in the perfect life of its chief cornerstone, Jesus Christ, and in His infinite Atonement and literal Resurrection. Jesus Christ has once again called Apostles and has given them priesthood authority. He invites all of us to come unto Him and His Church, to receive the Holy Ghost, the ordinances of salvation, and to gain enduring joy.

Two hundred years have now elapsed since this Restoration was initiated by God the Father and His Beloved Son, Jesus Christ. Millions throughout the world have embraced a knowledge of these prophesied events.

We gladly declare that the promised Restoration goes forward through continuing revelation. The earth will never again be the same, as God will “gather together in one all things in Christ” (Ephesians 1:10).

With reverence and gratitude, we as His Apostles invite all to know—as we do—that the heavens are open. We affirm that God is making known His will for His beloved sons and daughters. We testify that those who prayerfully study the message of the Restoration and act in faith will be blessed to gain their own witness of its divinity and of its purpose to prepare the world for the promised Second Coming of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ.

This proclamation was read by President Russell M. Nelson as part of his message at the 190th Annual General Conference, April 5, 2020, in Salt Lake City, Utah.

THE LIVING CHRIST

The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
